cur:catacombs-nunziatella-christ-judge.summary: Wilpert's photograph shows the damaged vault of a small chamber painted with concentric circles and compartments; in the central field Christ sits as judge, with figures turned towards him in the surrounding fields. The chamber took its name from this vault painting, an early attempt to picture the judgment of the soul by Christ.
facts: Italian Wikipedia calls the main monument of this small rural catacomb the 'cubiculum of the Judgment', fully painted and dating to the second half of the 3rd century.
The catacomb was discovered by Giovanni Battista de Rossi in 1877; it contains no martyrs' tombs and served a small rural community.
Painting reproduced from Joseph Wilpert, Die Malereien der Katakomben Roms (Freiburg, 1903) (plate 75).
cur:catacombs-nunziatella-christ-judge.notes: Much of the vault is lost; the identification of the central figure as Christ the Judge follows Wilpert and later scholarship.
